A.question: My client Maria Lopez works full time and runs a weekend cake business that has lost money every year since 2023. Can she deduct those losses against her wages, and how has the Tax Court treated side businesses like this? Her W-2 and intake memo are uploaded.

subqueries.query: activity not engaged in for profit deduction limitation
Tax Court treatment of side businesses with consistent losses and full-time employment
the client works full time and runs a weekend cake business that has lost money every year since 2023

answer.text:
Tax year: 2023

Part 1: activity not engaged in for profit deduction limitation
Maria Lopez's cake business has reported net losses of $4,100 for 2023 [intake-memo.pdf, p. 1]. Under 26 U.S.C. § 183(a), if an activity is not engaged in for profit, no deduction attributable to that activity shall be allowed except as provided in that section [26 U.S.C. § 183(a)-(d)]. The cake business may be considered an activity not engaged in for profit if it does not meet the criteria set forth in 26 U.S.C. § 183(d) [26 U.S.C. § 183(a)-(d)]. The presumption of profit motive applies if the gross income from the activity exceeds the deductions for three out of five consecutive years, which does not apply here as the business has incurred losses every year since 2023 [26 U.S.C. § 183(a)-(d)].

Part 2: Tax Court treatment of side businesses with consistent losses and full-time employment
In cases where taxpayers have full-time employment and operate a side business that incurs losses, the burden is on the taxpayer to substantiate the deductions claimed for that business [T.C. Memo. 2025-80, at *7-8].

T.C. Memo. 2025-80.note: No negative treatment found in CourtListener as of 2026-09-26. Pending appeals are not tracked.
